correctness.rationale: The bounded Bellman renewal operator has strict contraction modulus strictly below one. Its optimal value is attained by maximizing G_mu(t)/(1-A exp(-mu t)); differentiation gives a threshold curve with exact derivative a strictly negative derivative and endpoint range (0,1), proving a unique global solution for all positive decreasing gain rates. Strict Jensen and transform monotonicity prove convex-order comparison. The zero-mortality expansion follows from a regular implicit equation with nonzero slope at the classical optimum and finite third travel moments. Independent exact parameter calculations and a standard-library checker (2,311 assertions) are consistent. Limits and model hypotheses are stated.

value.rationale: Equal mean travel times are insufficient for lifetime-optimal patch-use decisions once death risk acts during travel; this is a biologically motivated information gap in the classical MVT. The theorem gives a usable distributional comparison for every strictly decreasing gain curve, a single Laplace-transform sufficient statistic and exact first-order variance sensitivity for low mortality, with a sharp exact two-law illustration. It is neither a mere renaming of a mean-rate criterion nor an arbitrary numerical special case. Its prediction is restricted to its explicitly idealized ecological model.
